setups.quote: We numerically benchmark the performance of the noise-tailored code versus nonoptimized CSS surface codes and demonstrate that (i) the sub-threshold logical error rates are exponentially suppressed as a function of the code distance and (ii) the threshold grows monotonically as noise becomes less uniform across qubits.
In particular, we compare their logical error rates under the condition that they consume a comparable amount of resource overhead.
We compare the decoding time of the surface code and that of the concatenated quantum Hamming code, ensuring both achieve a comparable logical error rate at a physical error rate of p = 0.01526.
To investigate the effect of correlated errors, we compare the logical error rates in the absence and presence of correlated errors.
We compare the logical error rates derived from assuming the absence and presence of correlated errors, as shown in Fig. 10.

We measure its effectiveness at dealing with syndrome measurements corrupted by radiation, and we observe how the logical error rate of separate logical qubits correlates with their position on the quantum chip.
